verdict.rationale: Smithery documents triggers that let an MCP server surface upstream events, which the server POSTs directly to the consumer. There is no evidence of user-defined rules or of Smithery automatically executing actions when events fire. Event delivery is a developer building block for constructing automation, not the rule-to-action capability itself, so it earns no credit.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Triggers let an MCP server surface events from its upstream service.
When the upstream provider fires, your server POSTs the event **directly to the consumer** — Smithery is not in the delivery path.
